outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no proof, disproof or claimed resolution of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for any tree has appeared in the sources I could find; the post-window events are partial results (a polynomial bound for bounded-boxicity graphs, a stable-set analogue, a polynomial bound for the single tree P5, an almost-all-graphs statement) and several variants that do not bear on the bullet, and Wikipedia (fetched; footer 'last edited 18 September 2026') still says the conjecture remains unproven.
problem_asks: (1) For every tree T, is the class of graphs with no induced T χ-bounded, i.e. does there exist a function f_T such that every graph G with no induced T satisfies χ(G) ≤ f_T(ω(G))? The question is a single universal claim over all trees T. (2) The bullet's wording is the χ-bounded form; the equivalent clique form (every graph with no K_t and sufficiently large χ contains every tree T as an induced subgraph) is stated in Wikipedia and is the same question. (3) Since every forest is an induced subgraph of a tree, the forest version is equivalent (per Wikipedia). The bullet does not ask for the polynomial binding-function version, the path-induced version, or the stable-set consequence; those are recorded below only as context.

events.what_happened: Gyárfás settled the conjecture for T a path. Wikipedia's partial-results list gives 'Paths: Gyárfás (1987)' and its reference is Gyárfás, 'Problems from the world surrounding perfect graphs', Zastosowania Matematyki 19 (1987) 413–441. Open Problem Garden says the path and star cases are an easy exercise. One search summary attributed the path case to Gyárfás's 1975 paper; I did not resolve this (see disputes).
events.delivers: χ-boundedness of T-free graphs for every path T.
events.remains: Every tree that is neither a path nor a star, subject to the partial results below.

checked_by.who: Zastosowania Matematyki (journal named in Wikipedia's reference)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper that Wikipedia cites for the path case; I did not read the paper

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, for paths only.

events.what_happened: Kierstead and Penrice, 'Radius two trees specify χ-bounded classes', J. Graph Theory 18(2) (1994) 119–129 (DOI 10.1002/jgt.3190180203, per a search snippet). Result: for every tree T of radius two, the class of T-free graphs is χ-bounded. Cited by Wikipedia, Open Problem Garden, and Davies–Yuditsky (2024). I did not obtain the paper itself.
events.delivers: χ-boundedness of T-free graphs for every tree T of radius at most two.
events.remains: Trees of radius three and above, except the families covered by the later results below.

checked_by.who: H. A. Kierstead and S. G. Penrice; Journal of Graph Theory (journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Authors of a peer-reviewed journal article
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the theorem in J. Graph Theory; I did not read the paper

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, for radius-two trees only.

events.what_happened: Scott, 'Induced trees in graphs of large chromatic number', J. Graph Theory 24(4) (1997) 297–311 (per Wikipedia's reference list). Result as stated by Wikipedia and Open Problem Garden: for every tree T, graphs containing no induced subdivision of T are χ-bounded. Open Problem Garden states this gives the conjecture for subdivisions of stars; I did not verify that step.
events.delivers: χ-boundedness of the class of graphs with no induced subdivision of a fixed tree T. That class excludes all subdivisions of T, so it is a smaller class than the T-free class in the bullet; the result is a weaker statement than the conjecture for T itself.
events.remains: The conjecture for trees T itself, outside the subdivided-star case that the sources list as settled.

checked_by.who: Alex Scott; J. Graph Theory (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the result; I did not read the paper

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, in a weaker form (subdivision-free classes).

events.what_happened: Martin, 'A note on a conjecture of Gyárfás', arXiv:1605.06638 (v1 21 May 2016, v2 25 May 2016). Shows that one member T of a particular family of radius-three trees is forced as an induced subgraph in every triangle-free graph of radius two with sufficiently large chromatic number. I read only the arXiv abstract page; the family is not named there.
events.delivers: For one tree T from a family of radius-three trees, and only for host graphs that are triangle-free with radius two, every such graph of large chromatic number contains T induced. This is a restricted-hypothesis case.
events.remains: The conjecture for all graphs (no radius or triangle-freeness restriction) and for the other trees in the family.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, under added hypotheses on the host graph.

events.what_happened: Kierstead and Zhu, 'Radius three trees in graphs with large chromatic number', SIAM J. Discrete Math. 17 (2004) 571–581 (DOI 10.1137/S0895480198339869, per a search snippet; SIAM page paywalled, not opened). Result: the conjecture holds for a class of radius-three trees in which every vertex adjacent to the centre has degree 2 (Open Problem Garden's wording). A search summary gives 'degree at most 2' for the same class, so the wording differs between sources.
events.delivers: χ-boundedness of T-free graphs for one family of radius-three trees (neighbours of the centre of degree 2), and also the (2,...,2)-multibroom case.
events.remains: All other radius-three trees and trees of radius four and above, except as covered by the later results below.

checked_by.who: H. A. Kierstead and Y. Zhu; SIAM J. Discrete Math. (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the theorem; I did not read the paper

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, for one family of radius-three trees.

events.what_happened: Chudnovsky, Scott and Seymour, 'Induced subgraphs of graphs with large chromatic number. XII. Distant stars', arXiv:1711.08612 (v1 23 Nov 2017). Abstract: proves the conjecture for two families of trees in which vertices of degree greater than two are not clustered closely together; these families include all double-ended brooms and two-legged caterpillars. The abstract also states the conjecture is still open, known for trees of radius two and subdivided stars.
events.revisions: v1 23 Nov 2017; a v2 exists (listed on arXiv); the v2 date was not captured.
events.delivers: GS for two families of trees with non-clustered high-degree vertices, including double-ended brooms and two-legged caterpillars. The exact family definitions were not captured from the text.
events.remains: Every tree outside those two families.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, for the two families of trees.

events.what_happened: Scott and Seymour, 'Induced subgraphs of graphs with large chromatic number. XIII. New brooms', arXiv:1807.03768 (v1 10 Jul 2018). Abstract: proves the conjecture for every (1,...,1,2,...,2)-multibroom, a common generalisation of the Kierstead–Penrice (1,...,1) case and the Kierstead–Zhu (2,...,2) case.
events.revisions: v1 10 Jul 2018; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: GS for multibrooms whose legs have length 1 or 2 (mixed), per the abstract.
events.remains: Multibrooms with other leg lengths, and all trees outside this family; Nguyen–Scott–Seymour (2024) say 'it is not known whether all multibrooms satisfy the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture'.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, for one family of trees.

events.what_happened: Scott and Seymour, 'Polynomial bounds for chromatic number. V. Excluding a tree of radius two and a complete multipartite graph', arXiv:2202.05557 (v1 11 Feb 2022). Abstract: strengthens the Kierstead–Penrice theorem: for a radius-two tree H and d ≥ 2, an H-free graph with no complete d-partite subgraph with parts of size t has chromatic number polynomial in t.
events.delivers: A polynomial-in-t bound for radius-two-tree-free graphs that also exclude K_d(t). This is a polynomial bound under an extra exclusion, a different hypothesis from the bullet.
events.remains: The bullet itself, i.e. the χ-bound for H-free graphs with no extra exclusion, and all radius-three and larger trees.
events.direction: Neighbouring: a stronger form of the radius-two case under an added hypothesis; does not settle the bullet.

events.what_happened: Chiba and Furuya, 'Ramsey-type problems on induced covers and induced partitions toward the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture', arXiv:2205.14466 (v1 28 May 2022). Abstract: settles Ramsey-type problems for the induced SP-cover number and induced SP-partition number (covers and partitions by induced stars and paths), which the authors present as analogues of the conjecture.
events.delivers: Results on two invariants defined by covering and partitioning with induced stars and paths. These are analogues, not χ-boundedness of T-free graphs.
events.direction: Neighbouring analogue; discounted for the bullet, which asks about χ.

events.what_happened: Nguyen, Scott and Seymour, 'A note on the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture', arXiv:2302.08922 (v1 17 Feb 2023, the only version listed). Theorem 1.2: for every rooted tree (T,r) and t ≥ 1, a graph with no clique of size t and sufficiently large χ contains a path-induced copy of (T,r), i.e. a copy in which every path from r is induced in G. The paper states the induced conjecture 'remains open'. Equivalently, graphs with no path-induced copy of (T,r) and no K_t are χ-bounded.
events.revisions: v1 17 Feb 2023 only, per the arXiv abstract page. A search summary says it appeared in Graphs and Combinatorics in 2024; I did not verify this.
events.delivers: A weaker statement: the subclass of graphs with no path-induced copy of (T,r) is χ-bounded. Any graph with an induced copy of T has a path-induced copy, so this class is contained in the T-free class and the result does not give the bullet.
events.remains: The induced version for every tree T, which is the bullet.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture, but as a weaker path-induced form; the bullet's induced form is stated as open.

events.what_happened: Davies and Yuditsky, 'Polynomial Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for graphs of bounded boxicity', arXiv:2407.16882 (v1 23 Jul 2024; no later arXiv version). Theorem 1: for every positive integer d and forest F, the class of intersection graphs of axis-aligned boxes in R^d with no induced F is polynomially χ-bounded. Published in Innovations in Graph Theory 3 (2026), 37–48 (received 18 Sep 2024, accepted 10 Dec 2025, published online 2 Apr 2026). The introduction says the conjecture is 'widely open and is only known for forests F with relatively simple components'.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 23 Jul 2024 only. IGT journal dates: received 2024-09-18, accepted 2025-12-10, published online 2026-04-02.
events.delivers: For each fixed d, and within the class of graphs of boxicity at most d (box intersection graphs in R^d), T-free graphs for every forest F have a polynomial χ-bound. Restricted to bounded boxicity.
events.remains: The conjecture for general graphs of unbounded boxicity, i.e. the bullet for every tree.

checked_by.who: Innovations in Graph Theory (journal of record); referees not named on the pages I read
checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal; the authors are experts in the area (Davies at Leipzig, Yuditsky at ULB per the journal page)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the article on 10 Dec 2025 and published it on 2 Apr 2026; refereeing is presumed by journal practice but the referee reports are not visible to me

events.time_since_posted: About 26 months since the arXiv posting; journal publication 2 Apr 2026.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: a polynomial χ-bound holds, in the bounded-boxicity class, for all forests. Does not contradict the conjecture, and does not settle it for general graphs.

events.what_happened: Nguyen, Scott and Seymour, 'Trees and near-linear stable sets', arXiv:2409.09397 (v1 14 Sep 2024; v2 18 Jul 2025). For a forest H, every {H,K_{k+1}}-free graph G has a stable set of size |G|^{1−o(1)}; the authors say they cannot prove the linear bound that the conjecture would imply. For a multibroom T, every {T,K_{k+1}}-free graph has a stable set of size c|G| (linear), and as a corollary the fractional chromatic number is bounded: χ*(G) ≤ c. Published in Combinatorica 45(5) (article 49, October 2025, per the Princeton portal). The paper says: 'It is not known whether all multibrooms satisfy the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture.'
events.revisions: v1 14 Sep 2024; v2 18 Jul 2025 (current arXiv version). Combinatorica 45(5), Oct 2025. The content of the v2 changes was not examined.
events.delivers: A stable-set bound |G|^{1−o(1)} for every forest, not linear. A linear stable-set bound and a bounded fractional-χ bound for multibrooms only. These quantities are stable-set size and fractional chromatic number, not χ itself; the multibroom χ-bounds were already known for the (1,...,1), (2,...,2) and mixed families.
events.remains: The linear stable-set bound for forests, which the conjecture would imply; the χ-boundedness of every tree; and whether every multibroom (of arbitrary leg lengths) satisfies the conjecture.

checked_by.who: Combinatorica (journal of record); the authors are Tung Nguyen, Alex Scott and Paul Seymour, who are not independent of the work
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the article in Combinatorica 45(5), October 2025, per the Princeton research portal; I did not open the journal page

events.time_since_posted: About 25 months since arXiv v1; about 12 months since Combinatorica publication.
events.direction: Partial and neighbouring: the paper proves a weaker stable-set bound for all forests and a linear bound for multibrooms, quantities that the conjecture would imply but that the bullet does not ask for. Does not settle χ-boundedness of any tree.

events.what_happened: Reed and Yuditsky, 'The asymptotic χ-boundedness of hereditary families', arXiv:2506.01070 (v1 1 Jun 2025). Theorem 2: for every tree T, almost all T-free graphs G satisfy χ(G) = ω(G), so failures form a vanishing fraction of T-free graphs as the number of vertices grows. Also results for cycles C_k (except C_6) and for C_6-free graphs (bounding function (1+o(1))w²/log w). The introduction says the conjecture 'remains open for most trees'. A SLMath seminar listing from May 2025 also mentions the tree result; I did not open it.
events.delivers: An asymptotic statement about almost all T-free graphs: for each tree T, the proportion of T-free graphs with χ > ω tends to zero. This is a statement about typical graphs, not a worst-case χ-bound for all T-free graphs.
events.remains: The worst-case χ-bound for all T-free graphs, which is the bullet.
events.direction: Neighbouring analogue (almost-all graphs); does not bear on the worst-case bullet.

events.what_happened: Aubian, Ibiapina, Kuffner, Naserasr, Pujol, Robin and Zhou, 'Extension of the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture to signed graphs', arXiv:2511.03335 (single version, 5 Nov 2025). Defines Gyárfás–Sumner sets of signed graphs, studies order-2 sets, and shows the possible order-2 sets are restricted (first member (K3,−) or (K4,−); second a linear forest). The paper calls the unsigned conjecture 'the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture' and does not explicitly say whether it is open.
events.delivers: Results for signed graphs with a balanced constant colouring; nothing about χ-boundedness of unsigned T-free graphs.
events.remains: The bullet, which concerns unsigned graphs and every tree.
events.direction: Analogue (signed graphs); neutral to the unsigned question.

events.what_happened: Rahimi and Mojdeh, 'Towards Esperet's Conjecture: Polynomial χ-Bounds for Structured Graph Classes', arXiv:2512.09186 (submitted 9 Dec 2025). Cites the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture as background. The main theorems give linear or polynomial χ-bounds for graph classes that forbid a tree together with other graphs, for example {P6, (2,2)-broom}-free graphs, and C4-free and p-flag-free graphs with a broom-type tree and K_d(t) excluded.
events.delivers: χ-bounds for classes defined by a tree together with additional forbidden graphs. Each theorem carries extra forbidden structures beyond a single tree.
events.direction: Neighbouring: forbids a tree plus other graphs, so it does not bear on the single-tree bullet.

events.what_happened: Tung H. Nguyen, 'Polynomial χ-boundedness for excluding P5', arXiv:2512.24907 (v1 31 Dec 2025; v2 20 Apr 2026; v3 11 May 2026; v4 11 Aug 2026, the version shown by arXiv). Theorem 1.3: there is d ≥ 2 such that every P5-free graph G satisfies χ(G) ≤ ω(G)^d. The paper says P5 is 'the smallest open case of the polynomial Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture' (its Conjecture 1.2) and that the result answers a 1985 question of Gyárfás about the order of the χ-binding function for P5-free graphs. The previous best bound was quasipolynomial, x^{O(log x / log log x)}. The author notes the method is unlikely to give a quadratic bound.
events.revisions: v1 31 Dec 2025; v2 20 Apr 2026; v3 11 May 2026; v4 11 Aug 2026. The changes between versions were not examined.
events.delivers: A polynomial χ-bound for P5-free graphs (exponent d not specified). P5 is a path on five vertices, for which χ-boundedness was already known (Gyárfás's path case), so this gives a polynomial bound for that single tree, which is the polynomial version of the conjecture for P5.
events.remains: The conjecture for every tree other than P5 (the bullet), and the polynomial version for every tree other than P5.
events.time_since_posted: About 9 months since v1 (31 Dec 2025 to 11 Oct 2026). No journal acceptance or outside verification found in my searches.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: a single tree (a path) satisfies a polynomial χ-bound. It is a stronger form of an already-known χ-bound for one tree, and does not touch the other trees.

events.what_happened: Cameron, Sintiari and Spirkl, 'A positive instance of Scott's Conjecture on induced subdivisions', arXiv:2602.11990 (submitted 12 Feb 2026). Proves Scott's conjecture on induced subdivisions when H is a complete bipartite graph plus one vertex with exactly two neighbours on one side (including K4 with two disjoint edges subdivided). The introduction mentions the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture as the converse for trees, describing it as conjectured by Gyárfás and Sumner that every tree-free class is χ-bounded, and does not claim it is resolved.
events.revisions: v1 12 Feb 2026 (the HTML fetched is v1).
events.delivers: Scott's induced-subdivision conjecture for a class of non-tree graphs H. Different forbidden structure (induced subdivisions of H) from a single tree.
events.remains: The bullet, which is not addressed.
events.direction: Neighbouring: a different forbidden structure; does not bear on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Nguyen and Oum, 'Ramsey-type χ-bounds for χ-bounded graph classes', arXiv:2605.08848 (submitted 9 May 2026). Theorems forbid a forest T together with a second graph H (complete multipartite or complete bipartite) and give χ(G) ≤ C·R(α(H), ω(G)+1) in the stated cases. The paper states that a linear bound for {T, mK̄_s}-free graphs would imply the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture, and that the single-tree case therefore remains open. The paper also states that, for a path P, graphs with no induced P and no induced C4 are linearly χ-bounded.
events.revisions: v1 9 May 2026 only, per the arXiv listing read.
events.delivers: χ-bounds for graphs excluding a tree or forest together with a second graph (complete multipartite or complete bipartite), under the stated conditions. No result for a single tree T.
events.remains: The single-tree case, which is the bullet.
events.direction: Neighbouring: two forbidden graphs; the single-tree case is stated as open.

events.what_happened: Chuet, Djelloul, La, Pirot and Zaredehabadi, 'A Domatic Analogue of χ-Bounded Graph Classes and the Gyárfás-Sumner Conjecture', arXiv:2606.02030 (submitted 1 Jun 2026). Defines DOM-bounded classes (domatic number unbounded in terms of minimum degree), conjectures that for connected H the H-free graphs are DOM-bounded exactly when H is a tree of diameter at most 3, and proves bounds for star-free graphs and cographs (P4-free graphs). The paper states the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture as its Conjecture 1 for comparison and does not claim to resolve it.
events.delivers: Results on the domatic number, not χ. Star-free graphs have domatic number Ω(δ/log δ); cographs have domatic number at least 1 + δ/2.
events.remains: The bullet, which concerns χ and is not addressed.
events.direction: Analogue (domatic number); neutral to the χ question.

disputes.summary: Year of the path case: Wikipedia and Davies–Yuditsky (2024) give Gyárfás (1987); one search summary attributed the path case to Gyárfás's 1975 paper. I did not resolve this against the 1975 paper.

Degree condition in the Kierstead–Zhu (2004) radius-three family: Open Problem Garden says every vertex adjacent to the centre has degree 2; a search summary says degree at most 2. The wording was not checked against the SIAM paper.

Framing of the P5 result: a search summary called P5 'the smallest open case of this conjecture'. The paper itself (Section 1) says P5 is the smallest open case of the polynomial Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture, and P5 is a path, whose χ-boundedness was already known from Gyárfás.

summary: I found no proof, disproof or claimed resolution of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for any tree since 26 January 2024, and no AI system tied to it in any source I could open. Wikipedia (fetched; footer 'last edited 18 September 2026') still calls the conjecture unproven, and the Open Problem Garden page (posted 2009) still lists it as open. The post-window results are partial. (i) Davies and Yuditsky (arXiv 23 Jul 2024; Innovations in Graph Theory 2026) prove a polynomial χ-bound for T-free graphs of bounded boxicity, for every forest; this is a restricted class. (ii) Nguyen, Scott and Seymour (arXiv 14 Sep 2024; Combinatorica Oct 2025) prove a near-linear stable-set bound for every forest and a linear one for multibrooms, with a fractional-χ corollary for multibrooms. They say they cannot prove the linear bound the conjecture would imply, and that it is not known whether all multibrooms satisfy the conjecture. These are stable-set and fractional quantities, not χ. (iii) Nguyen (arXiv 31 Dec 2025; four versions to Aug 2026) proves P5-free graphs satisfy χ ≤ ω^d for some d. P5 is a path, where χ-boundedness was already known, so this gives a polynomial bound for one tree; the paper calls P5 the smallest open case of the polynomial version. I found no outside check of it. (iv) Reed and Yuditsky (arXiv 1 Jun 2025) show that for every tree T almost all T-free graphs have χ = ω; this is asymptotic and does not bound χ for all T-free graphs. The remaining post-window papers are variants or neighbouring problems that I record as discounted: signed graphs (Aubian et al.), tree-plus-other forbidden classes (Rahimi–Mojdeh; Nguyen–Oum, which states the single-tree case is open), a Scott induced-subdivision case (Cameron–Sintiari–Spirkl), and a domatic analogue (Chuet et al.). The pre-window baseline is the Gyárfás path case (1987), Kierstead–Penrice (radius-two trees, 1994), Scott (subdivision-free classes, 1997), Kierstead–Zhu (one radius-three family, 2004), Distant stars (two tree families, 2017), New brooms (mixed-leg multibrooms, 2018), Scott–Seymour (polynomial version for radius-two trees, 2022), and Nguyen–Scott–Seymour's path-induced weakening (2023). Close calls: the P5 and stable-set results are partial progress on the bullet in one case each, and the question is whether a bullet asking for all trees counts a single-tree polynomial result as a case. I read it as a case of a different quantity (the polynomial exponent), not a settlement of the χ-boundedness bullet. Davies–Yuditsky is a case of the bullet only inside bounded boxicity. Reed–Yuditsky answers an almost-all question. Each is recorded so the judging pass can decide. Searches for AI involvement (OpenAI, Google DeepMind/Gemini/AlphaEvolve, Anthropic/Claude, GPT-5.5/5.6, Lean formalisation, Erdős-problem databases, Terence Tao's blog, Quanta) found no AI-related result on this conjecture. Several unrelated 2026 AI-math items came up (listed under dead_ends), and none names this problem. The one name collision to watch is the Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture, which has its own 2026 AI-related activity. The Erdős problem #738 (triangle-free graphs of infinite chromatic number contain every tree; attributed to Gyárfás) is a different-hypotheses version. Its erdosproblems.com page shows no status label, zero proof claims, and no mention of AI.
competing_reading: Read the post-2024 results as partial progress on the bullet, not as no change: a polynomial χ-bound for P5 (a path, so one tree) and a linear stable-set bound for multibrooms are new, and Davies–Yuditsky settles the conjecture for bounded boxicity. On that reading the status is 'partially settled, for several families', and the record's events are cases of the bullet. The strict reading is that the bullet asks for every tree, so each event either covers at most one tree or a restricted class, or answers a different quantity (stable sets, fractional χ, domatic number, almost all graphs, or polynomial exponents). The universal claim is then untouched, and the status is 'open, with partial results'.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of arXiv 2512.24907: the tail (Section 6 onward, Section 7, Section 8 and the acknowledgements) was not readable through my fetch, so the AI disclosure and any remarks on trees are unverified. (2) The published versions of Nguyen–Scott–Seymour (Combinatorica 45(5)) and Davies–Yuditsky (IGT 3, 2026), to confirm the journal pages and referee dates directly. (3) Any arXiv or journal item after 11 Oct 2026, or a published verification of the P5 polynomial bound. (4) The live erdosproblems.com page for #738, for its status label. (5) The Chudnovsky–Seymour 2014 JCTB 'Extending the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture' paper, which Wikipedia cites, to confirm that it concerns heroic sets and assumes the conjecture (a search snippet says so; I did not read it). (6) The Kierstead–Zhu SIAM text for the degree condition.

judgement.why: The statement asks whether T-free graphs are χ-bounded for every tree T, so settling it for a family of trees (paths, radius-two trees, the Kierstead–Zhu family, distant stars, mixed multibrooms, subdivided stars via Scott) is a case; all of these predate the snapshot. Every post-snapshot event changes the question instead: Davies–Yuditsky restricts the host graphs to bounded boxicity (different hypotheses, not a restriction to a subset of trees); Nguyen–Scott–Seymour bound stable sets and fractional χ rather than χ; Reed–Yuditsky is about almost all graphs; Nguyen's P5 result is the stronger polynomial form for a tree whose χ-boundedness was already known since 1987, so it adds nothing to the question as stated; the rest are signed, domatic, multi-exclusion or induced-subdivision analogues. The closest calls were Davies–Yuditsky (case vs variant) and P5 (case of the polynomial strengthening vs variant). I chose variant for both because neither proves χ-boundedness for any tree not already covered. No AI involvement was found in any event.
judgement.doubts: The P5 paper's tail and acknowledgements were not read, so its AI-disclosure check is incomplete. Scott 1997 is marked case because sources say it yields the subdivided-star case; its main theorem is a weaker subdivision-free form. Distant stars and New brooms may have journal versions that the record does not capture, so they are marked unreviewed.
